_comment: FLEET BASELINE. Start here, deploy to a pilot OU, run in monitor for two
weeks, then promote. Every threshold below is a starting point, not a
validated number -- the README says that about the detection rules and it
is equally true of enforcement modes.
Keys beginning with _ are stripped by the deployment scripts.
_comment_mode: enforce = v1 behavior: block-severity findings are refused, warn findings
get a confirm step. Use monitor for the first two weeks of any rollout --
you cannot tune a false-positive rate you have never measured, and the
fastest way to kill the project is to block legitimate work in week one.
_comment_unknown: Sites discovery finds that are not in the catalog. Monitor, deliberately.
A heuristic that blocks is a heuristic that will one day block the county
_comment_coverage: catalog = the ~99 shipped sites plus extraSites. Narrow permission ask,
discover = also run the heuristic detector on every page. Requires the
broad build (node tools/build.mjs --coverage broad) and force-install,
because the permission warning is not something to show a user.
_comment_stage: all = every prompt is staged for the nightly agent, which is what makes
the cumulative-disclosure pass in agent_client.py work. flagged-only
shrinks the review corpus considerably and loses that capability. Pick
deliberately and write the choice into your retention schedule.
_comment_categories: ONLY LIST CATEGORIES THAT DIFFER FROM defaultMode. This is not a style
categoryModes outranks defaultMode in the precedence chain. So a baseline
that spells out every category as "enforce" silently NEUTRALIZES every
departmental override: groupPolicies.legal sets defaultMode=strict, the
baseline's categoryModes.public_chat=enforce wins, and Legal quietly runs
at enforce while the policy file says strict. Nothing errors. The options
page shows the mode as enforce and everyone assumes the file is wrong
Restating the default buys nothing and costs that. List deviations only.
The two below are genuine deviations:
enterprise_ai / meeting_ai -- sanctioned tenant-bound tools are
monitored, not blocked. Blocking the internal assistant is how you
push people to their phones: the README's 'give people an approved
media_ai -- image/audio generation is warn fleet-wide, because the
prompt is usually a description rather than a record. Departments
that disagree (sheriff) raise it in their own overlay.
_comment_never: Pages where the extension reading composer text is ITSELF the privacy
problem. This list wins over every mode including strict. Add your
county's payroll, benefits, and case-management vendors before pilot --
the Tyler Technologies entries are there because a case management system
is exactly where an employee legitimately types an SSN all day.
